body: Nepali licence plates are typically long, with white being the most common color. Private vehicles use red plates, while public vehicles use black ones.

All road coverage in Nepal uses a low-quality camera, often called 'shitcam', characterized by brownish colors and sometimes a large circular blur. This type of coverage is also common in India and can be found in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
Nepal drives on the left side of the road.

Nepal uses the Devanagari script, recognizable by the horizontal line across the top of words. The characters ङ (ṅa) and ङ्ग (ṅga) are more common than in Hindi, and native Devanagari numbers are also frequently seen on signage.

Nepal uses square concrete poles in flat areas and thin metallic poles in mountains, often with a trident poletop. A concrete pole with a trident top and triangle supports is unique to Nepal, as is a square pole with 2 vertical insulators on the sides.
Nepal frequently uses outer yellow road lines, which can be dashed or solid. Solid outer yellow lines are particularly common in the eastern Bagmati province.
Nepal primarily uses black-and-white striped concrete bollards, often with a red marking on top and having 3 to 5 stripes.
Nepal features flat agricultural areas in the south and high-altitude mountain roads in the northern half.

Buildings in Nepal range from colorful multi-story structures to smaller houses made of concrete, brick, or thatch, often with tiled or tin roofs. A common feature on building facades is triangle-shaped decorations.
Nepal uses black-and-white striped signposts. Be aware that these are also found in India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Malaysia.
White-painted Buddhist stupas, sometimes featuring painted eyes, are a unique architectural feature found only in Nepal.
District names often appear on addresses in Nepal, frequently in English.
The geography of Nepal varies from almost completely flat in the far south near India to very high-altitude and mountainous in the central and northern regions.
The western hills of Nepal are recognizable by their dry landscape and exposed, sparsely vegetated hillsides.
Areca Palms, with their thin trunks and small crowns, are primarily found in the southeast of Nepal.
Canola, a crop with bright yellow flowers, is mostly found in southern pockets in the western half of Nepal.
Chir Pines, with their long needles and conical crowns, are common in Nepal's mountains, especially in the west and near Kathmandu. The eastern region is generally greener.
Grass with white, fluffy-looking tips is most commonly seen just southeast of Kathmandu.
Japanese cedar trees, identifiable by their great height and narrow, fluffy crowns, are found only in far eastern Nepal.
Tea Plantations are exclusively found in far eastern Nepal, in both mountainous and flat areas.
Rounded roof tiles are most common in the flat regions south of Kathmandu and also prevalent further west.
West Bengal style roof tiles, which are organized and have small diamond-shaped protrusions, are most common in the far west flat region. This also applies to half-rounded tiles.
Flat, square grey stone tiles are common south of Kathmandu, particularly around Birgunj and Janakpur. Unlike in similar-looking parts of India, these tiles are neat and square.
Less organized rectangular stone tiles are a common roofing material in western mountain towns and can also be found towards the center of the country.
Roofs made from corrugated metal sheets are most common in the area between Birgunj and Janakpur.

Dark concrete railings along the sides of roofs are found in parts of western Nepal, most commonly in the Tulsipur valley where they sometimes have a stair shape. Lower quality railings can be found in the westernmost regions.
Gable ends decorated with golden-painted carvings of religious figures are mostly found around Kawasoti, west of Bharatpur.
Fences made primarily of sticks, with varying build quality, are most common in the eastern plains of Nepal.
In the far east, look for sheet metal roofs with a distinctive triangular 'window' below the ridge and an outward-sloping section beneath it.
Large sheet metal hip roofs with a small protrusion below the ridge are found around Biratnagar in the east.
Sheet metal hip roofs with a very small protruding piece of metal at the ridge are found mainly west of and around Biratnagar.
Mosques in Nepal are concentrated in Muslim-majority areas in the south, including around Janakpur, Birgunj, Nepalgunj, and Biratnagar.
Small, round clay huts with thatched roofs are mainly found around Birgunj and are also common across the border in India.
Poles with a cross attached near the top are common in the east.
In Kathmandu, you can find poles with an asymmetrical crossbar that has a triangular attachment on top and a support bar below.
While green and black water tanks are common everywhere in Nepal, yellow water tanks are mainly found in the east.
An orange Google car can be found in several locations, including Nepalgunj (west), Madi (central south), Biratnagar (east), and Birtamod (far east).
An orange Google car with a blue ribbon on the front is found around Biratnagar.
A blue Google car is found around Pokhara, Birgunj, and Malangwa.
If the blue Google car has an antenna, you are likely around Pokhara.
A white car provides coverage in many areas, including around Butwal, on the H10 to Pokhara, on the H04 to Kathmandu, and around Itahari.
A car with a black spoiler is found just around Janakpur.
A regular grey car can be found around Kathmandu and to the southeast around Lahan.
A blocky grey truck provides coverage east of Birgunj and just south of Kathmandu.
A grey car with a visible backlight is found in multiple areas, including around Pokhara, Kathmandu, north of Malangwa, and east of Itahari.
A red car, often with a long antenna, is found in Kathmandu and north of Janakpur.
North of Siddhicharan in eastern Nepal, you'll find unique high-elevation hills with an abundance of dark green rhododendron bushes, which may have hard-to-see red flowers.
A foggy, gloomy road northwest of Bhimeshwor Municipality is home to the only natural forest dominated by East Himalayan fir, recognizable by its tall, dark trees.
A sketchy yellow/orange dirt road in a high-elevation landscape with high-elevation oaks can be found northeast of Phungling in far northeastern Nepal.
A dirt track in a northwest-bound valley, recognizable by the snow-capped mountains to the northwest, is located north of Khaptad National Park in western Nepal.
Trekker coverage in Nepal is limited to the northeast, in the area southwest of Mount Everest.
Green forests and trees are found in the southern parts of Nepal's trekker coverage.
Barren mountain trails are characteristic of the northern parts of the trekker coverage.
Much of the coverage near Namche Bazar is sunny, with trails running close to the treeline, often just above a forest.
